<translate>
<!--T:1-->
<code>combat.json</code> controls stamina, blocking and parrying, damage mitigation, knockback, Speed and the passive dodge, ki charging and the Ki Surge, combat flight, ki weapons and the compatibility layer for weapons from other mods. It is a file of its own: none of these values are part of <code>general-server.json</code>.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:2-->
The file lives at <code>config/dragonminez/combat.json</code>; its schema is defined in <code>CombatConfig.java</code>. For how combat plays out in game, see [[Special:MyLanguage/Combat|Combat]]; for how defense and mitigation are applied step by step, see [[Special:MyLanguage/Stats and Attributes|Stats and Attributes]]. Technique-specific tuning (cooldowns, cast times, sizes, destruction) lives in <code>techniques.json</code>, documented on [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills Config|Skills Config]].
</translate>

<translate>
== Core combat and status == <!--T:3-->
</translate>
{{See also|Combat|Strike Attacks}}
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:4--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:5--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:6--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>staminaConsumptionRatio</code> || <code>0.083</code> || <translate><!--T:7--> Stamina cost of a melee attack relative to its damage.</translate>
|-
| <code>blockStaminaCost</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:8--> Stamina cost of a blocked hit, relative to the damage blocked.</translate>
|-
| <code>knockdownDurationSeconds</code> || <code>30</code> || <translate><!--T:9--> How long a player stays '''knocked down''' when a hit would have killed them but the fight doesn't allow kills (party PvP, Friendly Fist, Shadow Dummy sparring, or a Namekian or Majin preparing an absorption).</translate>
|-
| <code>baselineFormDrain</code> || <code>80</code> || <translate><!--T:10--> Baseline value forms scale their energy drain against (see the per-form <code>energyDrain</code> on [[Special:MyLanguage/Custom Forms|Custom Forms]]). Also used to size the ki cost of ki weapons.</translate>
|-
| <code>killPlayersOnCombatLogout</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:11--> If a player logs out mid-combat, they die on their next login.</translate>
|-
| <code>strikeGlobalCooldownTicks</code> || <code>60</code> || <translate><!--T:12--> Shared cooldown after any strike attack, so owning several strikes doesn't let you chain them (halved when a strike misses).</translate>
|-
| <code>accurateMobBattlePower</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:13--> Calculates the Battle Power of non-DMZ mobs from their health, attack, armor, ranged attack and speed. When <code>false</code>, it is simply <code>max health + attack damage × 5</code>.</translate>
|}

|}

<translate>
== Speed and passive dodge == <!--T:61-->
</translate>
{{See also|Stats and Attributes|Skills}}
<translate>
<!--T:62-->
Speed comes from Resistance. Players with the [[Special:MyLanguage/Meditation|Meditation]] skill can automatically dodge basic melee attacks: against players you need to be faster than the attacker, against other enemies you need a higher Battle Power. A dodge costs stamina, and consecutive dodges get less likely.
</translate>

! <translate><!--T:63--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:64--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:65--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>enableSpeedSystem</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:66--> Master toggle for Speed (movement bonus, step assist and passive dodge).</translate>
|-
| <code>speedReferenceStat</code> || <code>10000.0</code> || <translate><!--T:67--> Effective Resistance that adds +1.0 Speed at full Power Release.</translate>
|-
| <code>transformedSpeedCap</code> || <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:68--> Extra Speed multiplier while transformed or using a stack form.</translate>
|-
| <code>speedMovementCap</code> || <code>3.0</code> || <translate><!--T:69--> Maximum movement-speed multiplier from Speed.</translate>
|-
| <code>speedStepAssistThreshold</code> || <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:70--> Speed from which you step up blocks without jumping.</translate>
|-
| <code>speedStepAssistBonus</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate><!--T:71--> Extra step height given by step assist.</translate>
|-
| <code>enableSpeedDodge</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:72--> Toggle for the passive dodge.</translate>
|-

|-
| <code>speedDodgeFullChanceSpeedRatio</code> || <code>2.0</code> || <translate><!--T:74--> How far beyond the required speed ratio (as a multiple) you reach the maximum chance.</translate>

|-

|-

|-

<translate>
== Ki charging and Ki Surge == <!--T:94-->
</translate>
{{See also|Combat}}
<translate>
<!--T:95-->
Charging ki (default {{Key|C}}) to full and '''keeping on charging''' fills the '''Ki Surge''' bar. When you first reach full ki you release a '''Ki Burst''' that pushes back weaker enemies around you. Once the bar is full you enter a '''Ki Surge''': a bigger burst damages and blows back everyone nearby (it can't kill), then for a while your ki attacks hit harder and fly faster, you charge, move, fly and attack faster, and your aura grows; but spending ki costs more and drains the bar. Being stunned ends the surge.
</translate>

|-
| <code>kiChargeInterruptLockTicks</code> || <code>10</code> || <translate><!--T:101--> Ticks you can't restart charging after being interrupted.</translate>
|-
| <code>enableKiSurge</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:102--> Master toggle for the Ki Burst and the Ki Surge.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiBurstRadius</code> / <code>kiBurstKnockback</code> || <code>8.0</code> / <code>1.4</code> || <translate><!--T:103--> Radius and push of the Ki Burst on reaching full ki (only enemies with lower Battle Power are pushed).</translate>
|-

|-

|-

|-
| <code>surgeDrainPerKiFraction</code> || <code>1.5</code> || <translate><!--T:107--> Spending ki during a surge also drains the bar (spending X% of max ki removes 1.5 × X% of the bar).</translate>
|-
| <code>surgeBurstDamageRatio</code> || <code>0.25</code> || <translate><!--T:108--> Surge burst damage as a fraction of your max ki (less with distance; never lethal).</translate>
|-
| <code>surgeBurstRadius</code> / <code>surgeBurstKnockback</code> || <code>10.0</code> / <code>2.2</code> || <translate><!--T:109--> Radius and push of the surge burst.</translate>

|-

|-
| <code>surgeAttackSpeedMultiplier</code> || <code>1.40</code> || <translate><!--T:115--> Attack speed multiplier during a surge.</translate>
|-

|}

<translate>
<!--T:117-->
An [[Special:MyLanguage/Android|Android's]] Absorption Barrier can also force a Ki Surge when it overflows (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Racial Skills|Racial Skills]]).
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:137-->
'''Melee windup.''' A melee swing lands a moment after you press attack: the windup is the swing animation's length × the attack's <code>upswing</code> value from its [[Special:MyLanguage/Weapon Attributes|weapon attributes]] × 0.95, between '''3 and 7 ticks'''. The server times the windup (with some tolerance for lag) and checks every target against the real attack hitbox and line of sight before the hit counts. You can't deal melee damage while blocking, and starting to block cancels a swing in progress.
</translate>

<translate>
== Ki weapons == <!--T:138-->
</translate>
{{See also|Skills}}
<translate>
<!--T:139-->
<code>kiWeaponsConfig</code> is a map keyed by weapon type (<code>blade</code>, <code>scythe</code>, <code>clawlance</code>): the Ki Blade, Ki Scythe and Ki Claw Lance unlocked by the [[Special:MyLanguage/Ki Manipulation|Ki Manipulation]] skill. Default value:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"kiWeaponsConfig": {
  "blade": {
    "baseDamage": 0.0,
    "kiScalingDamage": 0.25,
    "baseKiCost": 0.0,
    "kiScalingCost": 0.075,
    "attackSpeed": -2.4,
    "forcedColor": "#FFFFFF",
    "weaponCombo": "dragonminez:sword"
  },
  "scythe": { "baseDamage": 0.0, "kiScalingDamage": 0.45, "baseKiCost": 0.0, "kiScalingCost": 0.105, "attackSpeed": -2.8, "forcedColor": "#FFFFFF", "weaponCombo": "dragonminez:scythe" },
  "clawlance": { "baseDamage": 0.0, "kiScalingDamage": 0.65, "baseKiCost": 0.0, "kiScalingCost": 0.175, "attackSpeed": -2.6, "forcedColor": "#FFFFFF", "weaponCombo": "dragonminez:trident" }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:140-->
Each entry has these fields:
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:141--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:142--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>baseDamage</code> || <translate><!--T:143--> Flat bonus damage per hit.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiScalingDamage</code> || <translate><!--T:144--> Bonus damage = Ki Damage × this × (Ki Manipulation level × 0.1).</translate>
|-
| <code>baseKiCost</code> || <translate><!--T:145--> Flat ki cost per attack.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiScalingCost</code> || <translate><!--T:146--> Extra ki cost per attack = <code>baselineFormDrain</code> × this.</translate>
|-
| <code>attackSpeed</code> || <translate><!--T:147--> Vanilla-style attack-speed attribute modifier (negative is slower).</translate>
|-
| <code>forcedColor</code> || <translate><!--T:148--> Hex color string used to render the weapon's ki effect.</translate>
|-
| <code>weaponCombo</code> || <translate><!--T:149--> Moveset the weapon uses (a [[Special:MyLanguage/Weapon Attributes|Weapon Attributes]] id).</translate>
|}

| <code>playerRelationToPassives</code> || <code>HOSTILE</code> || <translate><!--T:162--> Default relation (<code>HOSTILE</code>, <code>NEUTRAL</code> or <code>FRIENDLY</code>) toward passive mobs not otherwise listed.</translate>
|-
| <code>playerRelationToHostiles</code> || <code>HOSTILE</code> || <translate><!--T:163--> Default relation toward hostile mobs not otherwise listed.</translate>
|-
| <code>playerRelationToOther</code> || <code>HOSTILE</code> || <translate><!--T:164--> Default relation toward anything else.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Fallback compatibility for third-party weapons == <!--T:165-->
</translate>
{{See also|Weapon Attributes|Special Weapons}}
<translate>
<!--T:166-->
When a weapon has no dedicated [[Special:MyLanguage/Weapon Attributes|Weapon Attributes]] entry, DMZ matches its item id against a list of regular expressions to infer a sensible weapon category. Only items with an attack-damage modifier are considered.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:167--> Key</translate> !! <translate><!--T:168--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:169--> What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>fallbackCompatibilityEnabled</code> || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:170--> Master toggle for this system.</translate>
|-
| <code>blacklistItemIdRegex</code> || <code>"pickaxe"</code> || <translate><!--T:171--> Item ids matching this regular expression are never treated as a DMZ-style weapon.</translate>
|-
| <code>fallbackCompatibility</code> || <translate><!--T:172--> 20 default entries (below)</translate> || <translate><!--T:173--> Ordered list of <code>{ item_id_regex, weapon_attributes }</code> mappings from regular expression to category; the first match wins.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:174-->
Default mappings (<code>item_id_regex</code> → <code>weapon_attributes</code> category):
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:175--> Regular expression</translate> !! <translate><!--T:176--> Category</translate>
|-
| <code>claymore&#124;great_sword&#124;greatsword</code> || <code>dragonminez:claymore</code>
|-
| <code>great_hammer&#124;greathammer&#124;war_hammer&#124;warhammer&#124;maul</code> || <code>dragonminez:hammer</code>
|-
| <code>double_axe&#124;doubleaxe&#124;war_axe&#124;waraxe&#124;great_axe&#124;greataxe</code> || <code>dragonminez:double_axe</code>
|-
| <code>scythe</code> || <code>dragonminez:scythe</code>
|-
| <code>halberd&#124;glaive&#124;pike&#124;lance&#124;naginata</code> || <code>dragonminez:halberd</code>
|-
| <code>spear&#124;trident&#124;pitchfork&#124;javelin</code> || <code>dragonminez:spear</code>
|-
| <code>battlestaff&#124;staff&#124;quarterstaff&#124;pole</code> || <code>dragonminez:battlestaff</code>
|-
| <code>katana&#124;uchigatana&#124;nodachi&#124;tachi</code> || <code>dragonminez:katana</code>
|-
| <code>rapier&#124;foil</code> || <code>dragonminez:rapier</code>
|-
| <code>dagger&#124;knife&#124;shiv&#124;dirk&#124;kunai&#124;karambit&#124;wakizashi&#124;tanto</code> || <code>dragonminez:dagger</code>
|-
| <code>sickle&#124;kama</code> || <code>dragonminez:sickle</code>
|-
| <code>soul_knife</code> || <code>dragonminez:soul_knife</code>
|-
| <code>claw&#124;katar</code> || <code>dragonminez:claw</code>
|-
| <code>wand</code> || <code>dragonminez:wand</code>
|-
| <code>mace&#124;hammer&#124;flail</code> || <code>dragonminez:mace</code>
|-
| <code>axe</code> || <code>dragonminez:axe</code>
|-
| <code>coral_blade</code> || <code>dragonminez:coral_blade</code>
|-
| <code>twin_blade&#124;twinblade</code> || <code>dragonminez:twin_blade</code>
|-
| <code>cutlass&#124;scimitar&#124;machete</code> || <code>dragonminez:cutlass</code>
|-
| <code>sword&#124;blade</code> || <code>dragonminez:sword</code> <translate><!--T:177--> (catch-all)</translate>
|}

{{Note|type=tip|title=<translate><!--T:178--> Precise control</translate>|text=<translate><!--T:179--> If you are adding a weapon mod's item and want precise control instead of relying on regular-expression inference, give it a real [[Special:MyLanguage/Weapon Attributes|Weapon Attributes]] entry. The datapack entry always wins over the fallback guess.</translate>}}

<translate>
== Reload and validate == <!--T:180-->
</translate>
{{See also|Reloading and Updating Changes|How to JSON}}
<translate>
<!--T:181-->
# Edit <code>config/dragonminez/combat.json</code>.
# Validate the JSON syntax.
# Run <code>/dmzreload config</code> (or <code>/dmzreload</code>).
# Test in-game: block and parry timing, ki weapon damage and cost, and (if relevant) a third-party weapon's inferred category.
</translate>
